_README: BOARDCFG-2026-09-13. THE single source of truth for the MLB board's draft and stake numbers.
Python owns this file. build15.py stamps it into D.meta.cfg on every build; index.html reads
D.meta.cfg and falls back to its own literals only when a board has no cfg (archived boards).
assemble_tickets.py imports it directly.
WHY: on 2026-09-13 ten of these were defined in BOTH index.html and assemble_tickets.py and
kept in sync by hand. Two had already drifted -- CHALK_N was 0 in the engine and 4 in the
fallback drafter, FLOOR was 41 vs 130. Nothing detects that; a divergence only shows up the
rare night the fallback actually runs, which is the worst possible time to find it.
TWO PER-GAME CAPS, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME KNOB. GAME_CAP (6) bounds bats per game in the
gated pool. RESERVE_GAME_CAP (4) bounds them in the RESERVE tier -- the sub-gate bats a moon
may reach for only when the gated pool cannot fill it. Tighter is deliberate. Both were bare
literals; three README/HANDOFF lines described the second as 'the span-fill fallback is still
4', which read like a stale GAME_CAP and was repeatedly mistaken for one. Naming it settles
that. Changing RESERVE_GAME_CAP moved no board on any slate tested (09-03, 09-07, 09-10,
08-27) because the reserve tier is rarely reached -- so treat it as live but seldom binding,
and do not conclude from a no-op test that it is dead.
NOT in here on purpose. DEADCODE-2026-09-22 finished what this paragraph started: GATE_N and
FAM_CAP are GONE from the code, not just kept out of this file. GATE_N was unread in both
drafters; FAM_CAP lived inside the Dingers mint, which was deleted whole -- it had been behind
`if(!DINGERS)return` since DINGERS-RETIRED-2026-08-25 and had not run in a month.
⚠️ FLOOR is NOT dead, and this file used to say it was. index.html's copy (41) was inert and is
deleted; assemble_tickets.py's (130) is LIVE -- it is the default at the `_floor = ... else FLOOR`
fallback. It stays out of this config because it is a fallback-path constant, not board shape.
Scoring weights are NOT here either: _SIG lives in build15.py, kas_weights_v1.json and
ev_weights_v1.json own the live model. This file is draft SHAPE and STAKE only.
ANCHOR_MAX_ODDS (ANCHORCAP-2026-09-22) is the ONE price rule on the parlay side, and it
binds ANCHORS ONLY -- moon legs are deliberately uncapped. Source: backtest15-priceband-
2026-09-13, the only price study run on REAL posted odds (17,932 priced bats, 80 slates).
Holding price constant, the model's top half out-hits its bottom half by +3.13pp at
zero, twice, on n=1,244 and n=1,860. Above +850 the test cannot even run (the model's top
half holds 68 bats, then 25). So 650 is where our measured ability to rank STOPS, and an
anchor is the seat that rides two moons and a builder. Measured across the 92 committed
slates, the cap binds on 21 of 814 anchors (2.6%), 19 of them in 2026-06-18..24, and NO
slate has fewer than 4 bats priced <= 650, so it cannot starve the board.
⚠️ daily15-2026-09-13 crowned a WIDER anchor band (+300..+1150) and it is not the one we
follow, because its book was synthetic -- its own doc says pricing off a second model
'manufactures edge that a real market would never hand over'. Real prices win.
CONFLOCK_SETTLE_MIN (CONFLOCKSETTLE-2026-09-22) is the one TIME rule on the lock. A posted card
is not trusted the instant it appears -- a ticket may not LATCH until the card behind every leg
has been standing for this many minutes. Source: claude/cardrevision-2026-09-22.md, which walked
11 slates of committed slate_auto pulls (09-12..09-22, 2,276 pulls). 273 sides posted a confirmed
nine; 10 of them were later REVISED -- 3.7%, about one per slate. Revision lag from first post:
24, 24, 25, 30, 30, 70, 83, 105, 110, 200 minutes (median 50). Cards post a median 180 min before
first pitch (min 113, p10 148), so the settling period is spent almost entirely on lead time we
already had. Trade measured at each N: 30 -> 5/10 revisions caught, 60 -> 5/10, 90 -> 7/10,
120 -> 9/10 with 60 min of median lock window still left, 150 -> 9/10 and no better. 120 it is.
⚠️ This does NOT unlock anything. LOCK IS A LATCH (2026-08-17): once `t.locked` is true it stays
true forever. The rule only delays the FIRST latch; a slip already locked on the prior board is
untouched. The clock half of the lock (`started()` -- first pitch) is also untouched, so a card
that posts unusually late still locks when its game begins. Set to 0 to disable.
